sourceIndex.meaning: Static navigation snapshot of tracked paths and candidate C# members, with owner-level links to logical-table review records. Links do not certify whole-file coverage or freshness. Every path still requires classification; no-hit files and inactive preprocessor regions need inspection. Refresh after source or inventory changes.

rules: Nonsense means arbitrary authored data with no supported mathematical or functional basis; a switch or fitted expression that merely recites arbitrary values is not a meaningful port. Genuine named dispatch/case selection remains permitted.
Only entries explicitly marked converted or retained have a disposition under this ticket.
Historical XML formulas and closed research issues are inputs, not reviewed dispositions.
Owner candidates must be split into separately indexed logical fields; aliases share one entry.

User-authorized switch/case conversion is valid when a table clearly represents fixed case selection or dispatch; preserve domain, compatibility exceptions and one independent proof per logical table.
Discover through source and call graphs only. Do not run research suites or gameplay to choose work.
No repository-wide completion claim: unlisted tables are unreviewed, not excluded.
Retain a lookup only if porting is impossible or would produce nonsense. Performance, complexity, table size and unknown historical-tool provenance are not retention reasons.

tables.domain: ushort health 0..6000; native eight unsigned little-endian thresholds selected by even byte offsets 0..14
tables.interpretation: First nonnegative signed 16-bit health-minus-threshold difference. Differences cannot overflow in supported health range. Adjacent $FFFF at $A5:96FF is unreachable.
tables.reviewedEvidence: Read all eight bank_A5.asm thresholds and CMP/BPL loop; complete production selector compared with original cartridge threshold scan for all 6001 health inputs.
tables.disposition: Remove threshold array and search; return 2*max(0,7-health/750) after preserving maximum-health validation.
tables.rationale: Uniform integer differences of 750 explain every threshold. Integer quotient directly expresses health bands; no floating point, fitting, interpolation or exceptional corrections needed. Exact multiples belong to higher band.
tables.proofTest: VerifyDraygonHealthPaletteDefinitions (existing test reused; installed color fixture supplied)

tables.domain: even ushort phase byte offsets 0..14 and all ushort health values 0..65535
tables.interpretation: Threshold words are unsigned little-endian. Subtraction wraps to 16 bits then tests sign. Offset 16 is caller-owned completion; odd or later offsets are rejected.
tables.reviewedEvidence: Read all eight bank_B3.asm thresholds and CMP/BPL/completion flow; complete production result compared with original cartridge thresholds for all 524288 phase/health pairs.
tables.disposition: Remove threshold array; compute 375*(8-phaseByteOffset/2) after offset validation and retain signed wrapped subtraction.
tables.rationale: Uniform integer differences of 375 exactly explain the threshold domain. A direct unsigned health comparison would change supported wrap behavior; formula changes only the selected threshold.
tables.proofTest: VerifyBotwoonHealthPaletteDefinitions (existing test reused; installed color fixture supplied)

tables.nativeIdentity: $A8:CCC9+10*i timer field of palette records; $A8:CC67 graphics hook
tables.domain: ushort byte offsets 0,10,20,30,40,50; normalization additionally accepts terminator offset 60
tables.interpretation: Six unsigned little-endian duration words interleaved with four color words. Native cursor advances ten bytes. Negative color word at $A8:CCFD resets cursor before reading the next timer.
tables.reviewedEvidence: Read all six bank_A8.asm records and native timer/advance/reset flow; compare every production duration to cartridge, verify terminator, rejected offsets and 193-call production cadence.
tables.disposition: Remove duration array; return record%3==0 ? 64 : 16 after existing alignment/range validation.
tables.rationale: Two exact repetitions of a three-record timing policy. Bounded modulo clearly names cadence and does not admit invalid inputs. Colors are separately owned presentation data, not covered by this disposition.
tables.proofTest: VerifyWorkRobotPaletteTimingDefinitions (existing test reused; duration rejection assertions extended)

velocity.algorithm: Eastern action selects packed FF50 (-176/256 pixel per frame); central and western actions select FF20 (-224/256). These are NTSC action operands, not the different PAL regional operands. Existing FX owner sign-extends then shifts eight bits into its 16.16 accumulator.
velocity.proof: VerifySpeedEscapeStageVelocities compares all three original packed operands and complete selector ownership.

geometry.algorithm: Twenty consecutive twelve-byte records each describe one four-cell run with zero continuation. Left/right caps are vertical; up/down caps horizontal. Pointer division selects orientation and frame, with the first four records representing cleared caps. Published visual IDs use named orientation cases and bounded frame numbers.
geometry.proof: VerifyGreyCapGeometry checks independent twenty-pointer and published-ID fixtures, original run headers/terminators, export order, DTO/reverse-ID shape, every ushort pointer/default result, ordinal ID rejection and integer cell bounds.

collision.algorithm: Clear caps have air collision. Closed caps begin with shootable C, then vertical-extension D or horizontal-extension 5. Opening cells are solid 8 except middle cells in final left/down frames, which explicitly become air; right/up final interiors remain solid, matching original data.
collision.proof: VerifyGreyCapCollision compares all eighty original high nibbles through calculated, DTO and export views, including asymmetric final frames.

visuals.algorithm: Vertical grey tiles advance one per frame from AE and add a 32-tile stride for middle cells. Horizontal tiles alternate tileset rows by frame parity and advance two tiles every two frames from B2, adding one for outer cells. Clear caps use corresponding border roles at 82/83. Mirror bits follow orientation and cap half.
visuals.proof: VerifyGreyCapVisuals compares all eighty original low-twelve-bit fields through calculated, DTO and export views.

greyDoorPhysicalDrawReview.consumers: Gameplay calculates four cells directly at the original run positions, preserving selected artwork fallback and physical collision separation. Import/export and artwork validation materialize temporary DTOs. There is no persistent physical table or generated cache. The separate selected stock visual dictionary is resolved under greyDoorStockVisualReview.
greyDoorPhysicalDrawReview.confirmation: Verification and ResourceAudit builds and --grey-door-plm-draws pass three independent physical-field proofs plus the existing guarded five door lifecycle paths, shared-clear visuals, custom-artwork streaming and installed artwork behavior. The previous combined physical-data comparison is consolidated into these proofs. Presentation source pin updated.
greyDoorPhysicalDrawReview.scope: Complete grey/clear physical layouts and published ID mapping. No retention exception. Selected stock artwork is resolved under greyDoorStockVisualReview; ordinary door programs remain separate work; full source audit stays active.

greyDoorStockVisualReview.source: NTSC J/U v1.0 low-twelve-bit visual fields in twenty records at 84:A677..A766; RoomPlmGreyDoorVisualCatalog factory, constructor, getter and identity; original physical calculation independently established under greyDoorPhysicalDrawReview
greyDoorStockVisualReview.algorithm: Stock creates an empty catalog. GetWord validates the exact pointer/cell domain and projects the calculated physical word. Constructor requires all twenty unique ordinal frame identities and four visual-only words each, then clones only frames that differ from the calculated stock. Selected custom artwork remains data; unchanged frames do not populate a generated cache.
greyDoorStockVisualReview.identity: Calculate selected words into a temporary four-word stack buffer and preserve original sorted-pointer, one-run-per-frame hash framing. Input enumeration order remains irrelevant; mirrored custom visual words remain accepted.
greyDoorStockVisualReview.domain: Twenty known frame pointers with cells 0..3. Unknown pointer throws InvalidDataException; invalid integer cell throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Missing, duplicate, differently cased, malformed or collision-bearing frames remain rejected. Caller mutation cannot affect changed or unchanged imported frames.
greyDoorStockVisualReview.proof: VerifyGreyDoorStockMapping reads all eighty original visual words from supported ROM using an independent twenty-pointer/ID fixture. Factory, reversed import and installed catalogs match every value and the original hash. Full ushort unknown-pointer rejection, integer cell bounds, mixed custom/stock hash, changed/unchanged mutation isolation and constructor rejection paths are covered by this single named proof. Prior duplicate missing-frame/collision-word constructor checks are consolidated.
greyDoorStockVisualReview.confirmation: Verification and ResourceAudit builds plus --grey-door-plm-draws confirm original stock values/hashes, guarded five-door lifecycle paths, live custom artwork and streaming, shared-clear behavior, installed overrides, stock refresh and manifest rejection. Existing focused entry point pins ROM SHA256. Presentation source pin and ownership description updated.
greyDoorStockVisualReview.scope: Grey-door stock visual mapping and content identity. No retention exception; ordinary door programs and the wider source audit remain active work.

residentDoorClosingSelectionReview.source: NTSC J/U v1.0 second instruction fields at bank-84 BAF4+4, C842..C89C six-byte headers +4, and C8CA+4. Pinned bank_82.asm E91C..E97B reads PLMEntries_instList2 at E973; pinned bank_84.asm names each matching header and closing program. Source revision 362be646929cf8e483f692b73a6561cfc2dc1d0d.
residentDoorClosingSelectionReview.algorithm: Explicit named cases select Bomb Torizo grey, four ordinary grey, four yellow, four green, four red and Mother Brain escape-gate closing programs. This is semantic dispatch, not a numerical curve or arbitrary chronology. All enumerates the same named identities in original ascending header order and calls Resolve without retaining a generated record cache.
residentDoorClosingSelectionReview.domain: Exactly eighteen ushort header identities; all other values throw InvalidDataException with the existing error text. Blue collision PLMs remain outside this resident selector. Preserve the public Count and internal record shape; enumerable consumers replace the former ReadOnlySpan length use.
residentDoorClosingSelectionReview.consumers: RoomPlmSystem.DoorClosing resolves the matched resident header after the existing block-position/persistence checks, then installs the closing pointer and timer without runtime cartridge access. No caller behavior or supported domain is broadened.
residentDoorClosingSelectionReview.proof: Reuse VerifyResidentDoorClosingDefinitions as the single proof. Independent explicit native header keys establish the full accepted set/order; each output is compared to the original ROM header+4 word. Every other ushort input is rejected. For all eighteen entries, the existing typed-population fixture loads the actual family and confirms the real transition installs the expected pointer with the source header+4 word absent from its sparse runtime bus. Two orientations absent from retail populations remain included through import-side native setup/first-list metadata.
residentDoorClosingSelectionReview.confirmation: Verification build and --lookup-resident-door-closing pass the original eighteen values, complete input domain and production redirect. The focused command pins supported ROM SHA256 and runs inside the existing protected console boundary.
residentDoorClosingSelectionReview.scope: Resident closing-list selection only. Program byte mappings remain separate owners; nonresident fallback selection is resolved under fallbackDoorClosingSelectionReview. No retention exception; the wider source audit remains active.

fallbackDoorClosingSelectionReview.status: converted: twelve compound fallback records removed
fallbackDoorClosingSelectionReview.source: NTSC J/U v1.0 8F:E68A..E6A1 Door_Closing_PLMs and each selected bank-84 header+2 first instruction. Pinned bank_82.asm E8EB..E91B doubles DoorDirection and selects the header only after resident closing fails. Source revision 362be646929cf8e483f692b73a6561cfc2dc1d0d.

headers.algorithm: Directions 0..3 select no actor; 4/5/6/7 select named right/left/down/up blue closers; 8..11 select the same escape-gate closing actor. Explicit semantic cases preserve the original orientation order without a generated cache.
headers.proof: VerifyFallbackDoorHeaders compares all twelve original native table words through GetDefinition and public GetHeader; both APIs reject all byte inputs 12..255.

initialLists.algorithm: Each blue closer selects its named closing instruction list; every gate direction selects the shared escape closing list. No-actor directions return zero for this field too.
initialLists.proof: VerifyFallbackDoorLists reads the header from the independent original table, then its native header+2 word, and compares all twelve initial-list results. Full invalid byte domain is also checked.

fallbackDoorClosingSelectionReview.consumers: RoomPlmSystem.DoorClosing obtains the same compound result for fallback admission and slot creation. Public GetHeader continues to project the selected header. Existing four zero records and four gate aliases are preserved; no direction masking or extrapolation expands the supported domain. Error type/text remains unchanged.
fallbackDoorClosingSelectionReview.confirmation: Verification build and --lookup-fallback-door-closing pass both native-field proofs and the existing actual spawning fixture for every supported direction with an empty runtime bus. The fixture asserts no actor for zero headers and exact installed header/list for the eight spawning cases. Earlier compound direct-value checks are consolidated into two named field proofs. Focused entry point pins supported-ROM SHA256 and avoids unrelated suites.
fallbackDoorClosingSelectionReview.scope: Fallback header and initial-list mappings only. No retention exception; instruction program payloads and the wider source inventory remain active work.

greyDoorProgramReview.status: converted: 420-byte ordinary grey-door program blob removed
greyDoorProgramReview.source: NTSC J/U v1.0 84:BE59..BFFC, four 105-byte orientation groups starting BE59/BEC2/BF2B/BF94; pinned bank_84.asm 362be646929cf8e483f692b73a6561cfc2dc1d0d. RoomPlmSystem.GreyDoors derives resident, activation, shot and opening addresses through these compiled readers; the common interpreter executes timed draws and control opcodes.

controls.algorithm: Shared semantic opcode positions select condition setup, room-bit handoff, links, sleep/goto, shot counter, sound and deletion. Closing draws clear/frame-three then frames two/one for two ticks and frame zero for one; flashing repeats three blue/grey pairs held three/four ticks; opening holds frames one/two/three for four ticks and clear for one.
controls.proof: VerifyGreyProgramControls compares all 224 original opcode/duration bytes.

draws.algorithm: Orientation advances clear records twelve bytes, grey groups forty-eight bytes and closed-blue flash groups sixty bytes. Bounded frame traversal selects closing/opening animation and alternating flash states.
draws.proof: VerifyGreyProgramDraws compares all sixty-four original draw operands.

targets.algorithm: Local links relocate by the 105-byte orientation group stride, selecting sleep, activation, hit, flash and opening state positions. Persisted-door handoff selects the existing named closed-blue orientation program.
targets.proof: VerifyGreyProgramTargets compares all twenty-four original branch/link operands.

callback.algorithm: Each orientation installs the named BD0F follow-link-on-shot callback.
callback.proof: VerifyGreyProgramCallback compares all four native callback words.

sounds.algorithm: Closing selects library-three sound eight; opening selects seven at their exact packed byte positions.
sounds.proof: VerifyGreyProgramSounds compares all eight original sound bytes.

hitCount.algorithm: Each orientation uses one hit to set the persistent door bit and enter opening.
hitCount.proof: VerifyGreyProgramHitCount compares all four original threshold bytes.

greyDoorProgramReview.domain: Exactly BE59..BFFC bytes and BE59..BFFB word starts. Preserve all 419 overlapping views, including cross-orientation words, and packed argument alignment. Each named proof checks every ushort byte/word ownership and zero rejected outputs, comparing its fields with the original supported ROM through direct and composed readers. Adjacent condition data and yellow-door program remain unclaimed. No runtime cartridge dependency or persistent generated cache.
greyDoorProgramReview.confirmation: Verification build and --grey-door-plm-draws pass all six original-field proofs and existing guarded closing, condition unlock, flashing, hit/open/delete, persisted-bit reload and custom-artwork checks across all four ordinary orientations. Earlier combined byte proof consolidated; command pins supported-ROM SHA256.
greyDoorProgramReview.scope: Complete four ordinary grey-door program groups. No retention exception; blue/coloured programs and the wider source inventory remain active work.

blueDoorProgramReview.source: NTSC J/U v1.0 84:C489..C54C, four 49-byte orientation groups; pinned bank_84.asm 362be646929cf8e483f692b73a6561cfc2dc1d0d. Shared compiled program reader serves opening, fallback closing and grey/coloured closed-blue handoffs.

controls.algorithm: Named sound, delete and BTS opcodes combine with bounded timed-draw sequences. Opening holds each of three frames six ticks then clear ninety-four. Closing starts clear, walks frames three/two/one at two ticks, and falls into a one-tick closed draw.
controls.proof: VerifyBlueProgramControls independently compares all 112 original opcode/duration bytes.

draws.algorithm: Orientation advances clear draws twelve bytes and closed-blue groups sixty bytes. Opening traverses three twelve-byte frames forwards, closing backwards, and handoff selects the closed base.
draws.proof: VerifyBlueProgramDraws compares all thirty-six original draw operands.

sounds.algorithm: Opening and closing select native library-three sounds seven and eight at their packed byte positions.
sounds.proof: VerifyBlueProgramSounds compares all eight native sound operands.

bts.algorithm: The closed handoff assigns the named left-blue BTS base plus orientation, preserving left/right/up/down values 40..43.
bts.proof: VerifyBlueProgramBts compares all four original behavior operands.

blueDoorProgramReview.domain: Exactly 196 bytes and 195 overlapping word starts, including cross-orientation words and packed-byte alignment. All four named proofs check every ushort ownership/default result and original fields through direct and composed readers. Preceding red-door data and following C54D setup code are excluded. No stored program/cache or runtime cartridge reads.
blueDoorProgramReview.confirmation: Verification build and --blue-door-plm-draws pass four native field proofs and existing production door animation, collision, custom-artwork and installed override checks. Prior combined program-byte proof consolidated. Existing command moved before unrelated suites and pins supported ROM SHA256.
blueDoorProgramReview.scope: Complete ordinary blue-door instruction interval only. Physical layouts are resolved under blueDoorPhysicalDrawReview; selected stock visuals and coloured programs and the wider audit remain active work. No retention exception.

blueDoorPhysicalDrawReview.source: NTSC J/U v1.0 84:A9A7..AA96, four five-record orientation groups including preceding closed physical aliases. Pinned bank_84.asm 362be646929cf8e483f692b73a6561cfc2dc1d0d names A9A7/A9E3 as eye-door conversions and AA1F/AA5B as unused horizontal counterparts; all remain supported.

geometry.algorithm: Each twelve-byte record is one four-cell run, vertical for left/right and horizontal for up/down, with zero continuation. Arithmetic selects orientation and alias/frame index. Preserve enumeration order: sixteen editable frames followed by four aliases. Published IDs remain orientation/frame names; aliases resolve to frame zero.
geometry.proof: VerifyBlueCapGeometry checks every ushort descriptor/DTO/VisualSource input, missing outputs, exact twenty-pointer order, sixteen editable identities, all native run headers/terminators, ordinal reverse IDs and integer cell bounds. Existing VisualSource cases are independently verified, including unchanged passthrough of unsupported pointers.

collision.algorithm: Frame zero starts shootable C, then extension D vertically or 5 horizontally. The preceding physical alias changes only its first cell to solid 8. Other animation cells are solid 8, except final vertical-frame middle cells which become air; horizontal final frames remain solid.
collision.proof: VerifyBlueCapCollision compares all eighty native collision fields through calculated, DTO and exported views, including unused aliases.

visuals.algorithm: Vertical tiles start at C, advance one per frame and add a 32-tile middle-row stride. Horizontal tiles start at 1C, alternate tileset rows by frame parity and advance two every frame pair, adding one for outer cells. Mirrors follow orientation and cap half; physical aliases use frame-zero visuals.
visuals.proof: VerifyBlueCapVisuals compares all eighty native low-twelve-bit words through calculated, DTO and export views.

blueDoorPhysicalDrawReview.consumers: RoomPlmSystem draws four calculated cells directly with the same selected-artwork fallback and physical collision separation. Import/export and artwork validation still receive temporary DTOs. No persistent physical dictionary/cache remains. Selected stock artwork is a separate pending mapping.
blueDoorPhysicalDrawReview.confirmation: Verification and ResourceAudit builds plus --blue-door-plm-draws pass the three native physical-field proofs and existing opening/closing/closed-cap, source-read guard, custom-artwork and installed override checks.
